set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which vibrio causes gastroenteritis from raw oysters, with serious complications in people with diabetes or liver disease?
opts: Vibrio cholerae
Vibrio cholerae causes cholera from contaminated water; the oyster-borne vibrio dangerous in diabetes or liver disease is Vibrio vulnificus.
Campylobacter jejuni
Campylobacter jejuni comes from water, milk, meat and chicken; the oyster-borne vibrio is Vibrio vulnificus.
Vibrio vulnificus
Correct: Vibrio vulnificus causes gastroenteritis from raw oysters, with serious complications in persons with diabetes or liver disease; it is one of the "flesh-eating" bacteria.
Vibrio parahaemolyticus
Vibrio parahaemolyticus causes gastroenteritis from raw seafood with symptoms similar to cholera; the oyster vibrio dangerous in diabetes or liver disease is Vibrio vulnificus.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which spirochete genus is especially noted for linear double-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid and plasmids?
opts: Vibrio
Vibrio is a comma-shaped curviform rod, not a spirochete; among the spirochetes, Borrelia is noted for linear deoxyribonucleic acid and plasmids.
Borrelia
Correct: most bacteria have circular chromosomes, but these narrow cells may carry linear double-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid and plasmids, especially Borrelia.
Treponema
Treponema is a spirochete with thin, regular coils, but the genus singled out for linear deoxyribonucleic acid and plasmids is Borrelia.
Leptospira
Leptospira has tight coils with hooked ends; the genus singled out for linear deoxyribonucleic acid and plasmids is Borrelia.

mis.Treponema: competing organism in the same group
mis.Leptospira: competing organism in the same group

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which organism causes Rocky Mountain spotted fever?
opts: Borrelia burgdorferi
Borrelia burgdorferi causes Lyme disease, another tick-borne illness; Rocky Mountain spotted fever is Rickettsia rickettsii.
Rickettsia rickettsii
Correct: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is a Rickettsia rickettsii zoonosis carried by dog and wood ticks, with a distinct spotted rash.
Rickettsia typhi
Rickettsia typhi causes endemic (murine) typhus, spread by fleas; Rocky Mountain spotted fever is Rickettsia rickettsii.
Rickettsia akari
Rickettsia akari causes rickettsialpox, spread by mite bite; Rocky Mountain spotted fever is Rickettsia rickettsii.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: How do spirochetes such as Treponema, Leptospira and Borrelia move?
opts: By one polar flagellum outside
A single polar flagellum belongs to the curviform bacteria such as Vibrio and Campylobacter; spirochetes move by endoflagella that lie inside the cell.
By pili that pull the cell
Pili are not how spirochetes move; their motility comes from endoflagella, found inside the cell beneath the outer membrane.
They are nonmotile
Spirochetes are motile; it is the rickettsias that are nonmotile rods or coccobacilli. Spirochetes move by endoflagella inside the cell.
By endoflagella inside the cell
Correct: spirochetes are motile by means of endoflagella, which are found inside the cell, in the periplasmic space beneath the outer membrane.

mis.By one polar flagellum outside: adjacent fact from the same lecture (curviform flagella)
mis.They are nonmotile: adjacent fact from the same lecture (rickettsias are nonmotile)

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which ticks transmit Lyme disease?
opts: Ixodes ticks
Correct: Borrelia burgdorferi is carried by the white-footed mouse and transmitted by Ixodes ticks.
Dog and wood ticks
Dog and wood ticks carry Rickettsia rickettsii, the cause of Rocky Mountain spotted fever; Lyme disease is transmitted by Ixodes ticks.
Body lice
Body lice carry Rickettsia prowazekii (epidemic typhus) and trench fever; Lyme disease is transmitted by Ixodes ticks.
Rat fleas
Fleas spread endemic typhus from rodents; Lyme disease is transmitted by Ixodes ticks.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which diseases is Helicobacter pylori linked to?
opts: Dental caries
Dental caries is acid damage to enamel by plaque bacteria; Helicobacter pylori causes stomach and duodenal ulcers.
Ulcers and gastric cancer
Correct: Helicobacter pylori causes most stomach and duodenal ulcers and is an apparent cofactor in gastric cancer.
Secretory diarrhea
Secretory diarrhea is the effect of cholera toxin and the Campylobacter enterotoxin; Helicobacter pylori causes ulcers and is a cofactor in gastric cancer.
Atypical pneumonia
Atypical pneumonia is caused by Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Chlamydophila pneumoniae; Helicobacter pylori causes ulcers.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: What is the reservoir of Chlamydia trachomatis?
opts: Birds
Birds are the source of Chlamydophila psittaci, the cause of ornithosis; Chlamydia trachomatis has a human reservoir.
Rodents
Rodents are reservoirs of Rickettsia typhi and Borrelia hermsii; Chlamydia trachomatis has a human reservoir.
Cattle
Cattle pass Campylobacter fetus between themselves; Chlamydia trachomatis has a human reservoir.
Humans
Correct: Chlamydia trachomatis has a human reservoir; its two strains cause trachoma and lymphogranuloma venereum.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which disease does Ehrlichia chaffeensis cause?
opts: Epidemic louse-borne typhus
Epidemic typhus is caused by Rickettsia prowazekii and carried by body lice; Ehrlichia chaffeensis causes human monocytic ehrlichiosis.
Mite-borne rickettsialpox
Rickettsialpox is caused by Rickettsia akari, spread by mite bite from mice; Ehrlichia chaffeensis causes human monocytic ehrlichiosis.
Human monocytic ehrlichiosis
Correct: Ehrlichia chaffeensis causes human monocytic ehrlichiosis, a tick-borne infection whose distribution is similar to that of Rocky Mountain spotted fever.
Rocky Mountain spotted fever
Rocky Mountain spotted fever is caused by Rickettsia rickettsii; Ehrlichia chaffeensis causes human monocytic ehrlichiosis, also tick-borne and found in similar places.
set1.cite: PAJ5200.Misc inf agents-2.pptx, Slide 46 and image on Slide 47

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: What is the bull's-eye rash at the site of the tick bite in Lyme disease called?
opts: Erythema migrans
Correct: erythema migrans is the bull's-eye rash at the initial tick-bite location in Lyme disease.
A gumma
A gumma is a lesion of tertiary syphilis that forms in organs years after infection, not a rash at a tick bite.
A hard chancre
A hard chancre is the lesion of primary syphilis at the site of inoculation, not the Lyme tick-bite rash.
Bacillary angiomatosis
Bacillary angiomatosis is a Bartonella infection in patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, not the Lyme tick-bite rash.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which chlamydial form is the infectious one released by the infected host cell?
opts: The reticulate body
The reticulate body is the noninfectious, actively dividing form inside host cell vacuoles; the infectious form is the elementary body.
The endospore
Chlamydias make no endospore (the resistant endospore is Coxiella's); their infectious form is the elementary body.
The inclusion body
The inclusion body is the mass of chlamydias seen inside an infected cell; the infectious form released is the elementary body.
The elementary body
Correct: the elementary body is small, metabolically inactive, extracellular and infectious, released by the infected host cell; the reticulate body is the noninfectious dividing form.

mis.The endospore: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Coxiella)

set1.cite: PAJ5200.Misc inf agents-2.pptx, Slide 56 and image on Slide 57

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which description fits Rickettsia?
opts: Wall-less, highly variable cells
Lacking a cell wall describes Mycoplasma; rickettsias have a Gram-negative cell wall.
Comma rods with one flagellum
Comma-shaped rods with one polar flagellum are Vibrio; rickettsias are tiny, nonmotile coccobacilli.
Tiny, nonmotile Gram-negative rods
Correct: rickettsias are obligate intracellular parasites with a Gram-negative wall, among the smallest bacteria, nonmotile pleomorphic rods or coccobacilli.
Large spirals with endoflagella
Large spiral cells moving by endoflagella describe Borrelia, a spirochete; rickettsias are tiny, nonmotile Gram-negative rods or coccobacilli.

mis.Wall-less, highly variable cells: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Mycoplasma)

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which organs does Leptospira interrogans target?
opts: Kidneys, liver, brain and eyes
Correct: leptospirosis targets the kidneys, liver, brain and eyes, and long-term infections may affect the kidneys and liver.
Stomach and duodenum
The stomach and duodenum are the targets of Helicobacter pylori, which causes ulcers; Leptospira targets the kidneys, liver, brain and eyes.
Lining of small blood vessels
Entering endothelial cells of the vascular lining is the rickettsia pattern; Leptospira targets the kidneys, liver, brain and eyes.
Gums and tooth sockets
The gums and tooth sockets are attacked in periodontal disease; Leptospira targets the kidneys, liver, brain and eyes.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Why might erythromycin or tetracycline be used to treat syphilis?
opts: They work better than penicillin
They are LESS effective than penicillin; they are the fallback when penicillin is contraindicated, as in a patient with an allergy.
The disease is tertiary
The stage is not what calls for them; erythromycin and tetracycline are used when penicillin is contraindicated, for example by allergy.
The patient is pregnant
Pregnancy is not the reason given; erythromycin and tetracycline are the fallback when penicillin is contraindicated, for example by allergy.
Penicillin is contraindicated
Correct: erythromycin and tetracycline are less effective than penicillin G or doxycycline but can be used when penicillin is contraindicated, for example by patient allergy.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which group is at highest risk of Q fever?
opts: Hikers in tick country
Hikers risk tick-borne disease such as Lyme disease; Q fever risk is highest for farmers, veterinarians and lab technicians.
Farmers and veterinarians
Correct: a Q fever vaccine is available, and veterinarians, farmers and lab technicians are at highest risk; historic cases most likely arose from contaminated milking barns.
Surfers and water-skiers
Surfers and water-skiers are named as at risk of leptospirosis from urine-contaminated water, not Q fever.
Owners of pet cats
Cat owners risk cat-scratch disease from Bartonella; Q fever risk is highest for farmers, veterinarians and lab technicians.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: In relapsing fever, what brings each bout of high fever back down?
opts: The tick detaching
The tick's departure does not end each bout; the fever falls when an antibody response controls the current antigenic form.
Loss of the endoflagella
Borrelia does not shed its endoflagella between bouts; the fever falls with each antibody response to the current antigen.
An antibody response
Correct: the initial antibody response at first reduces the fever, until a mutant Borrelia with a new antigen causes a relapse, and each new antibody response again reduces the symptoms.
Tetracycline taken by mouth
Tetracycline is the usual treatment, but the fall in fever between relapses comes from each new antibody response to the organism.
set1.cite: PAJ5200.Misc inf agents-2.pptx, Slide 24 and image on Slide 25

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: What does cholera toxin cause?
opts: Necrosis of vessel linings
Necrosis of the vascular lining is the rickettsial vasculitis; cholera toxin causes secretory rice water diarrhea.
Secretory, rice water diarrhea
Correct: cholera toxin causes electrolyte and water loss through secretory diarrhea, "rice water stool", and the dehydration leads to muscle, circulatory and neurological symptoms.
Bloody diarrhea from invasion
Vibrio cholerae is noninvasive; its toxin drives water and electrolytes out as secretory rice water diarrhea.
Ulcers of the stomach lining
Stomach and duodenal ulcers are Helicobacter pylori; cholera toxin causes secretory rice water diarrhea.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: How does a fetus acquire syphilis?
opts: From a tick bite in infancy
Ticks carry Borrelia and the rickettsias of spotted fever; Treponema pallidum reaches the fetus across the placenta.
From the mother's urine
Urine spreads Leptospira, which is shed by mammals; Treponema pallidum is passed sexually and across the placenta.
Across the placenta
Correct: congenital syphilis is a trans-placental infection of the fetus, causing nasal discharge, skin eruptions, bone deformation and nervous system abnormalities after birth.
Through the birth canal
Infection in the birth canal is how newborns get chlamydial inclusion conjunctivitis; syphilis reaches the fetus across the placenta.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: What do mycoplasmas require from host cell membranes?
opts: Adenosine triphosphate
Needing the host's adenosine triphosphate describes the chlamydial reticulate body; mycoplasmas require special lipids from host membranes.
Urea for urease
Urea is what Helicobacter pylori's urease converts to raise its local pH; mycoplasmas need special host lipids.
Peptidoglycan
Mycoplasmas have no peptidoglycan and take none from the host; what they require is special lipids from host membranes.
Special lipids
Correct: mycoplasmas naturally lack cell walls, are highly pleomorphic and require special lipids from host membranes.

mis.Adenosine triphosphate: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Chlamydia)
mis.Urea for urease: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Helicobacter)

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: How do newly hatched tick larvae become infected with Borrelia burgdorferi?
opts: By feeding on infected mice
Correct: newly hatched larvae become infected when they feed on small animals such as mice, which harbor the spirochete, and continue development through the first year.
By hatching from infected eggs
The larvae hatch uninfected and pick up the spirochete when they feed on mice; the eggs are laid in plant litter by adults from deer.
By feeding on deer
Deer are where nymphs mature into adults in the second year; larvae are infected by feeding on mice.
By biting infected humans
Humans are accidental hosts, not the source of the larvae's infection; larvae are infected by feeding on mice.

mis.By biting infected humans: accidental host mistaken for a reservoir

set1.cite: PAJ5200.Misc inf agents-2.pptx, Slide 26 and image on Slide 28

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: In veterinary medicine, how is Campylobacter fetus spread among domestic herd animals?
opts: As a sexually transmitted disease

Correct: Campylobacter fetus is a significant veterinary pathogen as a sexually transmitted disease of domestic herd animals, passed animal to animal in cattle, sheep and goats; how humans acquire it remains uncertain.
By tick bites in pastures
Ticks carry Borrelia and the spotted-fever rickettsias; Campylobacter fetus passes between herd animals as a sexually transmitted disease.
By fleas from rodents
Fleas from rodents spread endemic typhus; Campylobacter fetus passes between cattle, sheep and goats as a sexually transmitted disease.
By airborne barn particles
Airborne particles from barns spread Q fever (Coxiella); Campylobacter fetus passes between herd animals sexually.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which organism causes relapsing fever?
opts: Borrelia burgdorferi
Borrelia burgdorferi causes Lyme disease, carried by the white-footed mouse and Ixodes ticks; relapsing fever is Borrelia hermsii.
Rickettsia typhi
Rickettsia typhi causes endemic (murine) typhus, spread by fleas; relapsing fever is caused by Borrelia hermsii.
Leptospira interrogans
Leptospira interrogans causes leptospirosis, spread in mammal urine; relapsing fever is caused by Borrelia hermsii.
Borrelia hermsii
Correct: Borrelia hermsii causes relapsing fever, with recurrent febrile and afebrile cycles; Borrelia burgdorferi causes Lyme disease.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: How does a newborn acquire chlamydial inclusion conjunctivitis?
opts: Via the birth canal
Correct: inclusion conjunctivitis occurs as the baby passes through the birth canal, and it is prevented by prophylaxis.
Across the placenta
Trans-placental infection is how congenital syphilis is acquired; inclusion conjunctivitis is acquired in the birth canal.
From flies after birth
Flying insects belong to the setting of ocular trachoma in poor sanitation; inclusion conjunctivitis is acquired in the birth canal.
From a pet bird at home
Birds transmit Chlamydophila psittaci (ornithosis); inclusion conjunctivitis is acquired in the birth canal.
set1.cite: PAJ5200.Misc inf agents-2.pptx, Slide 58 and image on Slide 59

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which nonsyphilitic treponematosis is a superficial skin lesion that depigments and scars the skin?
opts: Yaws
Yaws enters a skin cut, causing a primary ulcer that seeds a second crop of lesions; the depigmenting, scarring lesion is pinta.
Bejel
Bejel is a deforming childhood infection of the mouth, nasal cavity, body and hands; the depigmenting, scarring lesion is pinta.
Relapsing fever
Relapsing fever is a tick-borne Borrelia infection with febrile cycles, not a skin lesion; the depigmenting lesion is pinta.
Pinta
Correct: pinta, caused by Treponema carateum, is a superficial skin lesion that depigments and scars the skin.

mis.Yaws: competing disease in the same group
mis.Bejel: competing disease in the same group

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: How does dental plaque damage tooth enamel?
opts: It blocks the tooth's blood
Plaque sits on the enamel surface; it damages enamel through the acid its bacteria produce.
Its bacteria make acid
Correct: plaque harbors masses of bacteria that produce acid, which dissolves the enamel, leading to dental caries.
Its bacteria make urease
Urease raises pH and belongs to Helicobacter pylori; plaque bacteria damage enamel by producing acid.
It hardens into the gums
Hardened plaque is calculus, which irritates the gums and causes gingivitis; enamel is dissolved by the plaque bacteria's acid.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which eye sign of tertiary syphilis eventually ends in loss of the light reflex?
opts: Inclusion conjunctivitis
Inclusion conjunctivitis is a chlamydial infection a baby acquires in the birth canal; tertiary syphilis gives the Argyll Robertson pupil.
Leptospiral conjunctivitis
Conjunctivitis is a sign of leptospirosis with sudden high fever; the tertiary syphilis eye sign is the Argyll Robertson pupil.
Argyll Robertson pupil
Correct: the Argyll Robertson pupil of tertiary syphilis is irregular in shape and eventually loses its light reflex.
Ocular trachoma
Ocular trachoma is a severe chlamydial infection that deforms the eyelid and cornea; the tertiary syphilis eye sign is the Argyll Robertson pupil.
set1.cite: PAJ5200.Misc inf agents-2.pptx, Slide 14 and image on Slide 14

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: In the progression of dental disease, which step leads toward gingivitis rather than toward caries?
opts: Calculus formation
Correct: after plaque forms, one branch is acidification and cavitation leading to caries; the other is calculus (tartar) formation, leading to gingivitis, periodontal disease and bone resorption.
Acidification and cavitation
Acidification and cavitation lead to dental caries and tooth destruction; the gingivitis branch begins with calculus formation.
Pellicle formation
Pellicle formation comes before plaque and leads to both branches; the gingivitis branch begins with calculus formation.
Damage to the enamel
Enamel damage is dental caries on the acid branch; the gingivitis branch begins with calculus formation.
set1.cite: PAJ5200.Misc inf agents-2.pptx, Slide 67 and image on Slide 66

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Why can Vibrio cholerae need a very large infectious dose?
opts: It must first multiply in urine
Shedding in urine is how Leptospira spreads; the cholera dose is high because the vibrios must pass through the stomach.
It must first form a spore
Vibrio cholerae forms no spore (an endospore is the Coxiella feature); the dose is high because the vibrios must pass the stomach.
It must first pass the stomach
Correct: the infectious dose can run very high because the vibrios must first pass through the stomach to infect the intestines.
It must first enter the blood
Vibrio cholerae never needs the blood; it is noninvasive and acts in the small intestine once it has passed the stomach.

mis.It must first form a spore: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Coxiella)

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: What do rickettsias need in order to be cultivated?
opts: Live host cells
Correct: rickettsias are very small intracellular parasites that require live cells for cultivation.
Blood agar alone
Being cultured on blood agar is said of Bartonella, a fastidious relative; rickettsias require live cells.
Host-membrane lipids
Special lipids from host membranes are what Mycoplasma requires; rickettsias require live host cells.
A salt-rich medium
Salt tolerance belongs to the seafood vibrios; rickettsias need live cells to be cultivated.

mis.Blood agar alone: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Bartonella)
mis.Host-membrane lipids: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Mycoplasma)
mis.A salt-rich medium: adjacent fact from the same lecture (seafood vibrios)

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Which lesions develop in tertiary syphilis?
opts: Hutchinson's teeth
Hutchinson's teeth are a sign of congenital syphilis, acquired across the placenta, not of the tertiary stage.
Gummas
Correct: tertiary syphilis can last 20 years or longer; neurological and cardiovascular symptoms develop and gummas form in organs.
Hard chancres
A hard chancre is the lesion of primary syphilis at the site of inoculation, not of the tertiary stage.
Palm and sole rashes
A red or brown rash on the palms and soles is secondary syphilis; the tertiary stage brings gummas.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set1.q: Helicobacter pylori's urease converts urea into which products?
opts: Glucose and nitrogen
Urease does not make glucose; it converts urea into ammonium and bicarbonate, raising the local pH.
Ammonium and bicarbonate
Correct: urease converts urea into ammonium and bicarbonate, which raises the local pH and lets the bacterium survive in the stomach.
Lactic acid and water
Acid production is what plaque bacteria do to dissolve tooth enamel; urease converts urea into ammonium and bicarbonate, which raise the pH.
Hydrochloric acid
Making acid would lower the pH; urease converts urea into ammonium and bicarbonate, raising the local pH.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which property lets the seafood vibrios live in coastal waters?
opts: Salt tolerance
Correct: the seafood vibrios are salt-tolerant inhabitants of coastal waters that associate with marine invertebrates.
Endospore formation
An unusually resistant endospore is made by Coxiella burnetii, not the vibrios; they live in coastal waters because they tolerate salt.
Lack of a cell wall
Lacking a cell wall is the Mycoplasma feature; the seafood vibrios live in coastal waters because they are salt-tolerant.
Urease production
Urease lets Helicobacter pylori raise its local pH in the stomach; the seafood vibrios are salt-tolerant.

mis.Endospore formation: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Coxiella)
mis.Lack of a cell wall: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Mycoplasma)
mis.Urease production: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Helicobacter)

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Why may primary syphilis go undiagnosed?
opts: No lesion forms at the entry site
A lesion does form: a hard chancre appears at the site of inoculation; it is missed because it often heals on its own.
Its rash stays hidden on the soles
The palm and sole rash belongs to secondary syphilis; primary syphilis is a chancre that may heal spontaneously and be missed.
Its organisms stay out of the blood
In the first two stages spirochetes are in the lesions and in the blood; primary syphilis is missed because the chancre heals by itself.
The chancre often heals on its own
Correct: the hard chancre at the inoculation site often heals spontaneously, so the illness may be missed while the organism spreads.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Chlamydophila pneumoniae causes an atypical pneumonia that is serious in which patients?
opts: Patients with immunodeficiency
Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome is the setting of Bartonella's bacillary angiomatosis; Chlamydophila pneumoniae pneumonia is serious in asthma.
Patients with asthma
Correct: Chlamydophila pneumoniae causes an atypical pneumonia that is serious in asthma patients.
Patients with diabetes
Diabetes or liver disease makes Vibrio vulnificus serious; Chlamydophila pneumoniae pneumonia is serious in asthma patients.
Women late in pregnancy
Late pregnancy is the risk for Campylobacter fetus; Chlamydophila pneumoniae pneumonia is serious in asthma patients.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: What sets the El Tor biotype of Vibrio cholerae apart from other strains?
opts: It is milder and rarely infectious
El Tor is the opposite: it survives longer and is more infectious than other strains.
It lacks the O and H antigens
Vibrio cholerae possesses unique O and H antigens; El Tor is set apart by surviving longer and being more infectious.
It survives longer and spreads more
Correct: the El Tor biotype survives longer and is more infectious than other strains.
It invades the intestinal wall
No Vibrio cholerae strain is described as invasive; El Tor stands out because it survives longer and is more infectious.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which animals are the reservoirs of Borrelia hermsii?
opts: Squirrels and chipmunks
Correct: the mammalian reservoirs of Borrelia hermsii, the cause of relapsing fever, are squirrels, chipmunks and wild rodents, and it is spread by ticks.
Domestic cats
Cats are linked to cat-scratch disease from Bartonella; relapsing fever's reservoirs are squirrels, chipmunks and wild rodents.
Cattle and sheep
Cattle, sheep and goats pass Campylobacter fetus between themselves; relapsing fever's reservoirs are squirrels, chipmunks and wild rodents.
Pet birds
Birds transmit Chlamydophila psittaci, the cause of ornithosis; relapsing fever's reservoirs are squirrels, chipmunks and wild rodents.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: By which routes is Treponema pallidum transmitted?
opts: Through mammal urine in water
Contact with urine-contaminated water spreads Leptospira interrogans; Treponema pallidum passes sexually and across the placenta.
By inhaling contaminated dust
Inhaled infectious particles spread Coxiella burnetii, the cause of Q fever; Treponema pallidum passes sexually and across the placenta.
Sexually and across the placenta
Correct: humans are the natural hosts of Treponema pallidum, which spreads by sexual and trans-placental transmission and cannot survive long outside the human host.
By ticks from mouse reservoirs
Ticks feeding on mice spread Borrelia burgdorferi, the cause of Lyme disease; Treponema pallidum passes sexually and across the placenta.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which three genera make up the spirochetes?
opts: Leptospira, Rickettsia, Borrelia
Rickettsia is a tiny obligate intracellular coccobacillus, not a spirochete; the third genus is Treponema.
Treponema, Campylobacter, Borrelia
Campylobacter is a curved or spiral rod with one polar flagellum among the curviform bacteria; the third spirochete genus is Leptospira.
Treponema, Leptospira, Borrelia
Correct: Treponema (syphilis and the nonsyphilitic treponematoses), Leptospira (leptospirosis) and Borrelia (relapsing fever and Lyme disease) are the spirochetes.
Treponema, Vibrio, Borrelia
Vibrio is a comma-shaped curviform rod with one polar flagellum, not a spirochete; the third genus is Leptospira.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which shape identifies Leptospira?
opts: Comma-shaped rods
Comma-shaped rods with one polar flagellum are Vibrio; Leptospira has tight coils with a bend or hook at the ends.
Gull-winged curved pairs
Curved rods in S-shaped or gull-winged pairs are Campylobacter; Leptospira has tight coils with hooked ends.
Tight coils with hooked ends
Correct: Leptospira has tight, regular individual coils with a bend or hook at one or both ends.
Large, loose, irregular coils
Large cells with 3-10 irregularly spaced coils are Borrelia; Leptospira has tight, regular coils with hooked ends.

mis.Comma-shaped rods: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Vibrio)
mis.Gull-winged curved pairs: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Campylobacter)

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which chlamydial disease deforms the eyelid and cornea and may cause blindness?
opts: Ocular trachoma
Correct: ocular trachoma is a severe infection that deforms the eyelid and cornea and may cause blindness.
Inclusion conjunctivitis
Inclusion conjunctivitis is the newborn's eye infection from the birth canal, prevented by prophylaxis; the blinding eyelid and corneal disease is ocular trachoma.
Lymphogranuloma venereum
Lymphogranuloma venereum disfigures the external genitalia and pelvic lymphatics; the blinding eye disease is ocular trachoma.
Ornithosis
Ornithosis is a bird-borne pneumonia from Chlamydophila psittaci; the blinding eye disease is ocular trachoma.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Why is penicillin not used against Mycoplasma?
opts: They form resistant endospores
A resistant endospore is the Coxiella feature; penicillin fails against Mycoplasma because it lacks peptidoglycan.
Their outer membrane blocks it
Mycoplasma has no cell wall at all; penicillin fails because no peptidoglycan is present.
They have no peptidoglycan
Correct: mycoplasmas naturally lack cell walls, so no peptidoglycan is present; they are treated with tetracycline or erythromycin instead.
They live inside host cells
Obligate intracellular life is the rickettsia and chlamydia habit; penicillin fails against Mycoplasma because it has no peptidoglycan.

mis.They live inside host cells: adjacent fact from the same lecture (obligate parasites)
mis.They form resistant endospores: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Coxiella)

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: What is Brill-Zinsser disease?
opts: Relapsing Borrelia fever
Relapsing fever is Borrelia hermsii, a spirochete; Brill-Zinsser is the recurrent form of epidemic typhus.
Recurrent epidemic typhus
Correct: Brill-Zinsser disease is the chronic, recurrent form of epidemic typhus, caused by Rickettsia prowazekii.
Milder flea-borne typhus
The milder flea-borne typhus is endemic typhus (Rickettsia typhi); Brill-Zinsser is the chronic recurrent form of epidemic typhus.
Tick-borne spotted fever
The tick-borne spotted fever is Rocky Mountain spotted fever; Brill-Zinsser is recurrent epidemic typhus.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: How is Q fever usually acquired?
opts: By sexual contact
Sexual contact spreads syphilis and Chlamydia trachomatis; Q fever is usually acquired by inhalation.
By inhalation
Correct: Coxiella's infectious material includes urine, feces, milk and airborne particles, and it is usually inhaled, causing pneumonitis, fever and inflammation of the liver.
By raw oysters
Raw oysters transmit Vibrio vulnificus; Q fever is usually acquired by inhaling infectious particles.
By louse feces
Louse feces rubbed into a bite spread epidemic typhus; Q fever is usually acquired by inhaling infectious particles.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which animal carries Borrelia burgdorferi?
opts: The domestic cat
The cat is linked to cat-scratch disease from Bartonella; Borrelia burgdorferi is carried by the white-footed mouse.
The pet parrot
Birds transmit Chlamydophila psittaci (ornithosis); Borrelia burgdorferi is carried by the white-footed mouse.
The dairy cow
Contaminated milking barns are linked to Q fever from Coxiella; Borrelia burgdorferi is carried by the white-footed mouse.
The white-footed mouse
Correct: Borrelia burgdorferi is carried by the white-footed mouse and transmitted by Ixodes ticks in a two-year cycle involving mice and deer.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: How is Campylobacter jejuni enteritis transmitted?
opts: Contaminated food and drink
Correct: Campylobacter jejuni is transmitted by beverages and food; water, milk, meat and chicken are common sources.
The bite of an infected tick
Ticks spread Borrelia and the spotted-fever rickettsias; Campylobacter jejuni comes from food and drinks such as chicken and milk.
The scratch of a pet cat
A cat's scratch transmits Bartonella; Campylobacter jejuni comes from food and drinks such as water, milk, meat and chicken.
Inhaled dust from barns
Inhaled particles spread Coxiella burnetii (Q fever); Campylobacter jejuni comes from food and drinks.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which set of findings fits acute leptospirosis?
opts: Fever, sore throat, palm rash
Fever, sore throat and a palm and sole rash are secondary syphilis; leptospirosis gives sudden fever, muscle aches and conjunctivitis.
Rice water stool, dehydration
Rice water stool and dehydration are cholera; leptospirosis gives sudden high fever, muscle aches and conjunctivitis.
Fever, chest pain, sore throat
Fever, chest pain and sore throat are Mycoplasma pneumoniae's primary atypical pneumonia; leptospirosis adds conjunctivitis to fever and aches.
Fever, aches, conjunctivitis
Correct: leptospirosis brings a sudden high fever, chills, headache, muscle aches, conjunctivitis and vomiting; long-term infection may affect the kidneys and liver.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: In the Lyme disease tick cycle, on which animal do nymphs mature into adult ticks that mate?
opts: Deer
Correct: in the second year nymphs feed on several hosts, including deer and humans; on deer they mature into adult male and female ticks, which mate, and the female lays eggs in plant litter.
White-footed mice
Mice are where newly hatched larvae become infected in the first year; nymphs mature into mating adults on deer.
Humans
Humans are accidental hosts that nymphs may feed on; the adults mature and mate on deer.
Wild birds
Birds are not part of this cycle (they carry Chlamydophila psittaci); adult ticks mature and mate on deer.

mis.Humans: accidental host mistaken for a maintenance host

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: In cholera, which way do water and electrolytes move across the intestinal cell?
opts: Out of the cell into the lumen
Correct: normally water and electrolytes are absorbed from the lumen into the blood; cholera toxin reverses this, so chloride, bicarbonate, sodium, potassium and water are lost into the lumen.
From the lumen into the blood
Lumen-to-blood movement is normal intestinal absorption; cholera toxin causes loss of water and electrolytes into the lumen.
Into the cell, which then swells
The water does not stay in the cell; under cholera toxin water and electrolytes leave into the intestinal lumen.
Out of the gut into the lymph
Cholera's losses are not into the lymph; water and electrolytes are lost into the intestinal lumen, producing secretory diarrhea.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which treponematosis starts as a primary ulcer in a skin cut that seeds a second crop of lesions?
opts: Primary syphilis
Primary syphilis is a hard chancre at the site of sexual inoculation; the skin-cut ulcer that seeds a second crop is yaws.
Yaws
Correct: yaws, caused by Treponema pallidum subspecies pertenue, invades a skin cut and causes a primary ulcer that seeds a second crop of lesions.
Pinta
Pinta is a superficial skin lesion that depigments and scars the skin, not an ulcer that seeds a second crop.
Bejel
Bejel is a deforming childhood infection of the mouth, nasal cavity, body and hands, not a skin-cut ulcer.

mis.Pinta: competing disease in the same group
mis.Bejel: competing disease in the same group
mis.Primary syphilis: competing disease in the same genus

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: This rash appeared around the site of a tick bite after a hike. Which organism causes it?
opts: Borrelia hermsii
Borrelia hermsii is tick-borne too, but relapsing fever is a pattern of febrile cycles, not an expanding bite-site rash.
Treponema pallidum
Treponema pallidum is spread sexually, not by tick bite; its rashes are on the palms and soles in secondary syphilis.
Borrelia burgdorferi
Correct: the bull's-eye rash at the tick-bite site, erythema migrans, is the sign of Lyme disease, caused by Borrelia burgdorferi.
Rickettsia rickettsii
Rocky Mountain spotted fever is also tick-borne, but it gives a distinct spotted rash, not one expanding patch at the bite site.

set2.alt: A large, round, evenly red patch on the skin of the upper arm.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which vectors carry Rocky Mountain spotted fever?
opts: Rat fleas
Fleas carry endemic typhus from rodents; Rocky Mountain spotted fever is carried by dog and wood ticks.
Dog and wood ticks
Correct: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is a Rickettsia rickettsii zoonosis carried by dog and wood ticks; the cycle runs between ticks and dogs, with humans infected by tick bite.
Ixodes ticks
Ixodes ticks transmit Lyme disease; Rocky Mountain spotted fever is carried by dog and wood ticks.
Body lice
Body lice carry epidemic typhus and trench fever; Rocky Mountain spotted fever is carried by dog and wood ticks.
set2.cite: PAJ5200.Misc inf agents-2.pptx, Slide 46 and image on Slide 49

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: A patient has this rash on both palms, with fever and a sore throat, a few weeks after a genital sore healed by itself. Which organism is the cause?
opts: Rickettsia rickettsii
Rocky Mountain spotted fever gives a spotted rash after a tick bite, with no preceding sore that healed; this history is secondary syphilis.
Borrelia burgdorferi
Lyme disease gives a bull's-eye rash at the tick-bite site, not a palm rash after a healed genital sore.
Chlamydia trachomatis
Chlamydia trachomatis causes urethritis, cervicitis and lymphogranuloma venereum, not a palm and sole rash with fever.
Treponema pallidum
Correct: a red or brown rash on the palms and soles with an upper respiratory-like illness, after a chancre that healed on its own, is secondary syphilis, caused by Treponema pallidum.
set2.cite: PAJ5200.Misc inf agents-2.pptx, Slide 9 and image on Slide 13
set2.alt: Both palms covered in scattered red-brown spots.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: For discovering which organism did Warren and Marshall receive the Nobel Prize in Medicine?
opts: Treponema pallidum
Treponema pallidum, the spirochete of syphilis, is not their discovery; Warren and Marshall discovered Helicobacter pylori.
Vibrio cholerae
Vibrio cholerae causes cholera; Warren and Marshall's Nobel discovery was Helicobacter pylori in ulcer patients' stomachs.
Coxiella burnetii
Coxiella burnetii causes Q fever; Warren and Marshall discovered Helicobacter pylori in stomach biopsies.
Helicobacter pylori
Correct: Warren and Marshall, Australian doctors, discovered Helicobacter pylori in stomach biopsies from ulcer patients and received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 2005.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which is the most commonly diagnosed of all diseases in humans?
opts: Chlamydia infection
Chlamydia is the first or second most prevalent sexually transmitted disease, not the most commonly diagnosed of all diseases; that is dental caries.
Gingivitis
Gingivitis is inflammation of the gums from calculus; the most commonly diagnosed of all diseases is dental caries.
Dental caries
Correct: dental caries, a slow progressive infection of irregular areas of the enamel surface, is the most commonly diagnosed of all diseases in humans.
Periodontitis
Periodontitis is infection that reaches the tooth socket and can lose the tooth; the most commonly diagnosed disease is dental caries.

mis.Chlamydia infection: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Chlamydia)

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: How does Helicobacter pylori survive in the stomach?
opts: Urease raises its local pH
Correct: Helicobacter pylori produces urease, which converts urea into ammonium and bicarbonate, raising its local pH so the bacterium can survive.
It forms acid-proof spores
Helicobacter forms no spores (an endospore is the Coxiella feature); it survives the stomach by making urease, which raises its local pH.
It hides inside host cells
Living inside host cells is the obligate intracellular habit of rickettsias and chlamydias; Helicobacter survives by raising its local pH with urease.
It lacks a cell wall
Lacking a cell wall is the Mycoplasma feature; Helicobacter survives in the stomach by raising its local pH with urease.

mis.It forms acid-proof spores: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Coxiella)
mis.It hides inside host cells: adjacent fact from the same lecture (obligate parasites)
mis.It lacks a cell wall: adjacent fact from the same lecture (Mycoplasma)

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: A camper who was bitten by a tick develops fever and the spotted rash shown. Which organism is most likely?
opts: Rickettsia rickettsii
Correct: a tick bite followed by fever and a distinct spotted rash is Rocky Mountain spotted fever, caused by Rickettsia rickettsii; its early rash may be mistaken for measles.
Borrelia burgdorferi
Lyme disease is tick-borne too, but its rash is one expanding bull's-eye patch at the bite, not a spotted rash.
Rickettsia prowazekii
Rickettsia prowazekii causes epidemic typhus, carried by body lice rather than ticks.
Treponema pallidum
Treponema pallidum is spread sexually, not by tick bite; its rash is secondary syphilis on the palms and soles.

set2.alt: A wrist and hand covered in many small, flat, red spots.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Why is tetracycline a treatment for so many different bacteria, from Borrelia to Mycoplasma?
opts: Peptidoglycan synthesis blockade
Acting on peptidoglycan is why penicillin fails against Mycoplasma, which has none; tetracycline targets the prokaryotic 30S ribosomal subunit.
Selective Gram-negative wall attack
Tetracycline acts on ribosomes, not on cell walls; it is very broad-spectrum, targeting the prokaryotic 30S subunit.
Replacement of lost electrolytes
Electrolyte replacement is rehydration therapy, as in cholera; tetracycline is an antibiotic targeting the prokaryotic 30S ribosomal subunit.
Broad spectrum, 30S ribosome target

Correct: tetracycline is a very broad-spectrum antibiotic that targets prokaryotic ribosomes, at the 30S subunit; it is named for relapsing fever, Lyme disease, cholera, Q fever, Bartonella and Mycoplasma.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which stage of syphilis begins with a hard chancre at the site of inoculation?
opts: Congenital
Congenital syphilis is the fetal infection acquired across the placenta, shown by snuffles, skin eruptions and bone deformation, not a chancre.
Primary
Correct: primary syphilis is the appearance of a hard chancre where the organism entered; the chancre often heals on its own.
Secondary
Secondary syphilis brings fever, headache, sore throat and a red or brown rash, including the palms and soles, after the chancre has gone.
Tertiary
Tertiary syphilis is the late stage of gummas and neurological and cardiovascular disease, years after the chancre.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Which complications can genital Chlamydia trachomatis infection cause?
opts: Hutchinson's teeth
Hutchinson's teeth are a sign of congenital syphilis; genital Chlamydia trachomatis leads to pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility.
Salpingitis and infertility
Correct: as a sexually transmitted disease, Chlamydia trachomatis causes urethritis, cervicitis, salpingitis (pelvic inflammatory disease), infertility and scarring.
Gummas and heart disease
Gummas and cardiovascular disease are tertiary syphilis; genital Chlamydia trachomatis causes pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility.
Bacillary angiomatosis
Bacillary angiomatosis is a Bartonella infection in acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, not a chlamydial genital complication.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: Who is most at risk of infection with Campylobacter fetus?
opts: People with asthma
Asthma makes Chlamydophila pneumoniae's atypical pneumonia serious; Campylobacter fetus strikes debilitated persons and late pregnancy.
Women late in pregnancy
Correct: Campylobacter fetus is an opportunistic pathogen that infects debilitated persons or women late in pregnancy, with meningitis, pneumonia, arthritis and newborn septicemia.
Surfers and water-skiers
Surfers and water-skiers are at risk of leptospirosis from urine-contaminated water; Campylobacter fetus strikes debilitated persons and late pregnancy.
People with liver disease
Diabetes or liver disease makes Vibrio vulnificus serious; Campylobacter fetus strikes debilitated persons and women late in pregnancy.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire miscellaneous bacterial agents of human diseases
set2.q: How is endemic typhus spread to people?
opts: Louse feces rubbed into bites
Louse feces rubbed into the bite spread epidemic typhus (Rickettsia prowazekii); endemic typhus is spread by fleas.
The bite of a dog tick
Dog and wood ticks carry Rocky Mountain spotted fever; endemic typhus is spread by flea feces rubbed into the skin.
The bite of an immature mite
Immature mites spread scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi); endemic typhus is spread by fleas.
Flea feces rubbed into the skin
Correct: Rickettsia typhi is harbored by mice and rats and spread by fleas; flea feces are rubbed into the skin (or inhaled), so it occurs where fleas are heavy.
